name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page. It’s the fastest way to let keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks without cluttering the interface. The trade-off is a small visual footprint that stays visible at all times, but this is outweighed by universal usability gains.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users missing the skip link entirely if it’s always visible—it becomes noise, not utility. A better alternative is a skip link that only appears on keyboard focus, then fades away, preserving accessibility without visual clutter. Settle it with user testing: measure how often sighted keyboard users use it versus how often screen reader users rely on it.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a skip link that only appears after the first tab press and hides until the next tab cycle. This keeps the interface clean for mouse users while ensuring keyboard users see it when they need it—no visual noise, no missed opportunities. The trade-off is a tiny bit of JavaScript to track focus state, but that’s a fair cost for precision. User testing will confirm if the timing feels right.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users missing the skip link if it’s hidden until the first tab press—many won’t know it exists until they stumble into it. A better alternative is a skip link that’s always visible but visually subdued (low contrast, small size) until focus arrives, then it sharpens to full contrast. Settle it with user testing: measure how often keyboard users notice and use it in both versions.
